column3: “The soul of Jonathan was bound” is rendered “was knit.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“In his love for him” is rendered “because he loved him.”
“His garments” is rendered “his armor,” and NASB supplies “including.”
Close to the Hebrew; “good in the eyes” is rendered “pleasing in the sight.”
“Three-stringed instruments” (Hebrew וּבְשָׁלִשִׁים) is rendered “musical instruments”; the exact instrument is uncertain.
“Who were playing” is rendered “as they played”; “struck down” becomes “slain.”
“It burned to Saul” is rendered “Saul became very angry,” and “yet for him only the kingship” as “Now what more can he have but the kingdom?”
“Looking at David” is rendered “looked at David with suspicion.”
“Rushed” is rendered “came mightily,” and “prophesied” as “raved.” “As a day in a day” becomes “as usual.”
“He said” is rendered “he thought,” and “went around” as “escaped.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew; NASB adds “in” to “went out and came in.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Was afraid of” is rendered “dreaded.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Son of strength” is rendered “a valiant man,” and “Saul said” as “Saul thought.”
The Hebrew reads “who are my kinsfolk”; NASB renders “what is my life,” reading the word differently.
“At the time of giving” is rendered “at the time when … should have been given.”
Close to the Hebrew; “someone told” is rendered “When they told.”
“Saul said” is rendered “Saul thought,” and “in two” as “For a second time.” The meaning of “in two” is uncertain.
Close to the Hebrew.
“In the ears of David” is shortened to “to David.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Bride-price” is rendered “dowry.”
Close to the Hebrew; NASB carries “Before the days had expired” into verse 27.
“Gave them in full” is rendered “gave them in full number.”
Close to the Hebrew; NASB links the verse to verse 29 as one sentence.
“All the days” is rendered “continually.”
NASB supplies “to battle,” and renders “was successful” as “behaved himself more wisely.”
